entries.reason: the release's own AVMetadataItem has this key, value, keySpace and locale - the port's 8.0 file reads all four without defining them - so the member is added as a category with its storage attached, and the filtering is over identifiers the 8.0 file computes
entries.effect: the items whose identifier the filter's list names, in order; an empty list keeps everything, which is what the header's own +metadataItemFilterForSharing answers, and a nil array answers nil - both measured against the host, which answers nil from the identifier filter and an empty array from the shared-filter one
entries.source: whether any held release already carries it: every held cache, all fifteen: 4.3, 6.1.3, 7.0, 7.1, 7.1.1, 7.1.2 and 8.0 (armv7), 8.1.3, 8.2 and 8.4.1 (armv7s), 9.3.6 (armv7), 10.0.1, 11.0 and 12.0 (arm64) and 16.0 (arm64e), dumped with tools/corpus/dump-cache.lua and searched for the row's own symbol - a class and its metaclass, a method's _OBJC_METHOD_$_ name, an ivar's _OBJC_IVAR_$_ name - with _NSFileSize planted as a control, which answers 4.3 on this set so a run that answers nothing for it is a broken measurement; and the behaviour, and every default: the differential in tests/backports/host/avf-metadata, which links one probe twice - Apple's framework alone, and the port's objects beside it in one binary with the port's own classes renamed - and joins the two tables row by row, holding a ~ row about the port's own construction against the unmutated baseline

entries.reason: the first HELD RUNG that exports this class is 7.0, measured over all fifteen held rungs - 4.3 and 6.1.3 do not export it and 7.0 does - and `_NSFileSize` is planted as a control. So on a 6.1.3 band the release has no such class and the port DEFINES it, in AVMetadataItemFilter.m, under Apple's own name; from 7.0 up the release's own class answers and the port's definition is dropped by the band's staging, while the port's 7.0-era members - in AVMetadataItemFilter7.m, a category, which defines no symbol - are kept and land on whichever class is in the binary
entries.effect: answers the identifier list it was built with, under the 7.0 spelling -identifiers and the current -allowList - from ONE stored list, so the two generations cannot disagree; an empty list is what a filter with no identifiers answers
